newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FIVE SHARE LEAD AFTER SECOND ROUND OF BUICK CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FIVE SHARE LEAD AFTER SECOND ROUND OF BUICK CHALLENGE.

text.p: Defending champion Fred Funk drove and putted with precision to earn a five-way share of the second-round lead at the Buick Challenge on Friday.

Funk, statistically the most accurate driver on the PGA Tour this year, did not miss a fairway in a bogey-free seven-under-par 65, equal to the day's lowest round in intermittent rain at Callaway Gardens.
He was joined at 10-under 134 by fellow Americans John Maginnes (66), Davis Love (68), Michael Bradley (68) and Len Mattiace (68), one shot ahead of Brad Faxon, Fred Couples and Marco Dawson.
Funk, brimming with confidence after winning last week's B.C. Open, was delighted with everything except his iron play.
"I struggled with my irons all day, but aimed at the fat part of the greens when I had to," said Funk, 40, winner of four PGA Tour events.
"I played pretty conservatively but rolled in some putts. I putted exceptionally well."
Four of his seven birdies came from outside 20 feet.

Love, meanwhile, had one eye on the weather late in his round. "I was trying to get to 11 under in case it rains all weekend," said Love, aware of the possibility of the event being shortened due to the bad weather.

His goal over the next two weeks is to improve from his current ninth position on the PGA Tour money list. He wants to have a chance of standing at number one going into the season-ending Tour Championship.
Bradley said he was playing in a more relaxed frame of mind since his first child was born five months ago.
"It puts everything in perspective. Sure I want to play well, but if I play bad, so be it," he said.

Eighty-five players made the cut, which fell at one-under 143. Among those to miss it were John Daly, who slumped with a 77 for two-over 146, Payne Stewart, Fuzzy Zoeller, Justin Leonard, Mark Brooks, David Duval and Curtis Strange.
